# Sampling and splitting

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Array extensions

- `func sample(_ count: Int, replace: Bool = true, seed: UInt64) -> [Element]` — Draws a single random sample of `count` elements from the array. Returns: An array of `count` drawn elements. Empty if the array is empty or `count <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func trainTestSplit(testRatio: Double, seed: UInt64) -> (train: [Element], test: [Element])` — Splits the array into training and testing subsets using a seeded shuffle for reproducible results. Returns: A named tuple of `(train: [Element], test: [Element])`.
- `func kFoldIndices(k: Int, seed: UInt64) -> [(train: [Int], validation: [Int])]` — Partitions the array's sample positions into `k` train/validation folds for cross-validation, using a seeded shuffle for reproducible results. Returns: An array of `k` named tuples `(train: [Int], validation: [Int])`, each holding sample indices into this array and any parallel array. *(since 1.3.0)*

## Array extensions where some RandomNumberGenerator: RandomNumberGenerator

- `func sample(_ count: Int, replace: Bool = true, using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator) -> [Element]` — Draws a single random sample of `count` elements from the array, drawing from a caller-supplied random number generator. Returns: An array of `count` drawn elements. Empty if the array is empty or `count <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*

## Array extensions where L: Hashable

- `func stratifiedSplit<L>(labels: [L], testRatio: Double, seed: UInt64) -> (trainFeatures: [Element], testFeatures: [Element], trainLabels: [L], testLabels: [L]) where L : Hashable` — Splits paired feature and label arrays into training and testing subsets, preserving the class distribution from the labels in both sets. Returns: A named tuple of `(trainFeatures, testFeatures, trainLabels, testLabels)`.

## Array extensions where Element == [Double]

- `func oversample(labels: [Int]) -> (features: [[Double]], labels: [Int])` — Balances an imbalanced dataset by generating synthetic samples for smaller classes. Returns: A tuple of `(features, labels)` with all classes balanced to the majority count.

## Array extensions where Element == Double

- `func resampled(iterations: Int = 1000, seed: UInt64, statistic: ([Double]) -> Double) -> [Double]` — Returns the resampled distribution of a statistic. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the statistic computed on each resample. Empty if the input array is empty or `iterations <= 0`. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func samplingDistribution(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, seed: UInt64, statistic: ([Double]) -> Double) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of an arbitrary statistic. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the statistic computed on each sample. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func samplingDistribution(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator, statistic: ([Double]) -> Double) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of an arbitrary statistic, drawing from a caller-supplied random number generator. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the statistic computed on each sample. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfMean(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, seed: UInt64) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample mean. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample means. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfMean(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample mean, drawing from a caller-supplied random number generator. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample means. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfMedian(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, seed: UInt64) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample median. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample medians. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfMedian(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample median, drawing from a caller-supplied random number generator. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample medians. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfStandardDeviation(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, seed: UInt64) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample standard deviation. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample standard deviations. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func samplingDistributionOfStandardDeviation(sampleSize: Int, iterations: Int = 1000, using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator) -> [Double]` — Returns the sampling distribution of the sample standard deviation, drawing from a caller-supplied random number generator. Returns: An array of length `iterations` containing the sample standard deviations. Empty if `self` is empty, `iterations <= 0`, or `sampleSize <= 0`. *(since 1.3.0)*
